title: Bring ResultStore and large tool-result persistence to parity
objective: Upgrade Go's oversized tool-result persistence to match TS behavior for thresholds, JSON/text content, empty results, preview stability, and error handling.
implementation_scope: Support text and structured text-block content persistence with .txt and .json extensions.
Skip image and non-text structured content persistence.
Inject an explicit empty-output marker for empty or whitespace-only tool results.
Use stable create-once semantics for existing persisted files so repeated turns produce byte-identical previews.
Implement tool-specific threshold resolution with hard opt-out for infinite/max-unbounded tools where Go has the metadata.
Return useful filesystem error messages while preserving original content on persistence failure.
out_of_scope: Do not implement stateful per-message aggregate budget in this task.
Do not change tool execution semantics beyond result block post-processing.
acceptance_criteria: Tests cover large text result, structured text result, image result skip, empty result marker, existing file replay, and write failure fallback.
Persisted-output wrapper format stays compatible with TS summary and budget recognition.
The query loop continues to store large results before adding tool messages to history.
risks: Go type definitions may not distinguish all content block shapes currently handled by TS.
Changing preview text can affect prompt cache stability; keep exact strings stable once introduced.
dispatch_prompt: Upgrade Go ResultStore to TS-equivalent large tool-result persistence, including JSON/text handling, empty-result markers, and stable preview replay.
